claims.text: A force-matched interatomic potential trained on extensive, representative high-temperature ab initio MD data will accurately capture the complex many-body interactions in liquid equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The force-matched potential will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by about 40% relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
The force-matched potential will predict free energies within 10 meV/atom of direct ab initio calculations.
The applicable material is equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi in both liquid and near-melting solid states.
The applicable temperature window is Tm ± 50 K, described as approximately 1600–2100 K.
The potential will be fitted directly to ab initio MD force data from high-temperature simulations.
A broad and diverse database of liquid configurations should be used for training.
The trained potential will produce atomic-force distributions that reflect local many-body interactions and subtle variations among liquid configurations.
Direct force matching will make the potential mimic the ab initio force landscape.
Mimicking the ab initio force landscape will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved representation of liquid many-body interactions will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
Many-body interactions govern the dynamics and entropy of the liquid state.
Conventional EAM potentials are used as the reference baseline.
TOR-TILD's unmodified EAM references do not fully capture the liquid's configurational diversity.
Extension of the method to HEA compositions other than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi requires verification of comparable configurational sampling.
The degree of mismatch reduction and free-energy accuracy depends on the completeness of the ab initio training set.
Failure to sample rare or complex configurations may reduce the predicted improvement.

contradictions.description: A single-alloy window of Tm ± 50 K spans only about 100 K, whereas the stated approximate range of 1600–2100 K spans 500 K; the relationship between that broad range and the claimed ±50 K window is not resolved.
